item.title: Educational Immersion for All: Accessibility and Inclusion in eXtended Reality
item.content:encoded:
Andrea Antonio Cantone, University of Salerno

Dragan Ahmetovic, University of Milano

Paloma Diaz, Universidad Carlos III de Madrid

Giuliana Vitiello, University of Salerno

This special issue explores how immersive technologies such as Virtual Reality, Augmented Reality, and Mixed Reality can be designed and implemented to create equitable educational experiences that serve all learners. While immersive technologies offer significant potential for engaging students through interactive, embodied learning, many current applications lack adequate accessibility and inclusive design considerations, potentially creating new digital divides.

The special issue welcomes interdisciplinary research integrating perspectives from human-computer interaction, educational technology, accessibility research, and learning sciences. It seeks contributions investigating how immersive technologies can support diverse learners, including students with disabilities, neurodivergent learners, and individuals from varied cultural and socio-economic backgrounds.

Original research articles, empirical studies, case studies, and evidence-based methodological analyses addressing accessibility challenges, design frameworks, adaptive systems, evaluation methods, and inclusive practices in XR educational environments are invited for submission.

Appel publié par Behaviour & Information Technology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Design and development of accessible and inclusive immersive learning and training environments
  • Inclusive design frameworks and guidelines for immersive educational technologies
  • Immersive technologies supporting students with disabilities (e.g., cognitive, sensory, motor, neurodevelopmental conditions)
  • Adaptive and personalized immersive learning and training experiences
  • Accessibility challenges and solutions in XR educational interfaces
  • Use of immersive technologies to support neurodivergent learners
  • Evaluation methods for accessibility, usability, and user experience in immersive educational systems
  • Immersive technologies for social skills training and behavioral learning
  • AI-driven adaptive systems in immersive learning environments
  • Multimodal and embodied interaction techniques for accessible XR learning
  • Immersive simulations for inclusive education and special education
  • XR technologies for experiential and collaborative learning in inclusive classrooms
  • Ethical, social, and accessibility implications of immersive technologies in education

item.title: Human-AI Interaction in Intelligent Workplaces: Behaviour, Trust, Experience, and Human-Centered Design
item.content:encoded:
Muhammad Imran Rasheed, University of Surrey

Barbara Rita Barricelli, Università degli Studi di Brescia

Waseem Ul Hameed, Universiti Utara Malaysia

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence systems are transforming workplace interactions, employee behavior, and organizational dynamics. While prior research has focused on AI adoption and performance outcomes, this collection addresses the human-centered dimensions of AI at work, including how employees develop trust in intelligent systems, experience AI-mediated processes, adapt their behaviors, and navigate issues such as technostress, autonomy, and cognitive load.

The special issue prioritizes behavioral, cognitive, and psychological perspectives on human-AI interaction in organizational settings. It seeks contributions that explore employee experiences with intelligent technologies, design of user-centered AI systems, transparency mechanisms, and the creation of psychologically sustainable digital work environments. The collection welcomes empirical, theoretical, and design-oriented research across quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-method approaches.

item.title: Persuasive Technology 2026
item.content:encoded:
Elena Vlahu Gjorgievska, University of Wollongong

Kiemute Oyibo, York University

Yugo Nakamura, Ritsumeikan University

The special issue will include selected papers from the 21st International Conference on Persuasive Technology. The special issue will be by invitation only.

This special issue is by invitation only. Invited papers must have at least 35% extra content from the conference paper. The additional content cannot be related work only or an extended discussion, but should include at least 35% of new results.

item.title: Smart systems and the governance of sociotechnical transformation
item.content:encoded:
Wanhao Zhang, Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

Younghoon Chang, University of Nottingham Ningbo China

Sameer Kumar, University of Malaya

Smart systems are now deeply embedded in various social contexts, functioning as sociotechnical arrangements that sense, classify, predict and intervene in everyday practices. This special issue seeks to understand how these digitally enabled systems reshape relations between humans, machines, organisations and institutions, and how they become consequential through design, institutional embedding and everyday use.

The issue addresses both how smart systems are governed and how they themselves participate in governing sociotechnical transformation. Key concerns include questions of behaviour, interaction, coordination, authority, accountability and power, particularly examining hybrid intelligence and human-AI collaboration. The special issue invites submissions examining smart systems not merely as technical innovations but as systems shaping governance, interaction and behaviour in organisational, institutional and everyday contexts.

Appel publié par Behaviour & Information Technology. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Smart systems in homes, workplaces, healthcare, education, mobility, public services and platform-mediated environments
  • Human-centred AI, hybrid intelligence and human-AI collaboration in organisational and everyday settings
  • Conceptual, methodological and design-oriented approaches to studying governance in smart systems
  • Algorithmic decision-making, coordination, compliance and accountability
  • User adaptation, negotiation, resistance, appropriation and trust in relation to smart technologies
  • AI ethics, information privacy, surveillance, transparency and asymmetrical power in digital systems
  • Smart and digital health, care technologies and digitally mediated wellbeing
  • Digital work, algorithmic management, robotic management and the reconfiguration of organisational routines
  • Datafication, monitoring, prediction and automated feedback as modes of governance
